## Natural history notes

A tiny concealer moth characterized by narrow gray-brown to tan wings with scattered black markings or speckling that give it the “black-marked” appearance. In Florida, it has been recorded in wooded and semi-wooded habitats, including forested sites such as Ocala National Forest and coastal areas such as Hobe Sound. Adults are small, mostly nocturnal, and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed concealed on plant or detrital material, contributing to the broader food web as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and other insect-eating animals.
